A race by construction, so the file is not in the stable list: the result depends on whether all five first snapshots (each superseded once by the color-grid custom element) have landed when the page draws, about 100 ms after load. Until 2026-10-16 the polyfill always lost it (TIMEOUT in every rep); since its first snapshot is one round it wins it on a warm load (fresh-browser loop: first load TIMEOUT 7 of 7, later loads PASS 8 of 8) and in full runs lost, half won (FAIL) or won (PASS) rep 1 while reps 0 and 2 timed out. onpaint-remove-drawable-element.tentativ.note: needs synchronous rasterisation: a userland snapshot is an SVG image decoded asynchronously (the first lands frames after a change; native paints in the rendering update of the change). One-frame wait, see onpaint.tentative.html. 'report drawable ancestor': the removal is committed and painted (changedElements []) one frame before the rebuilt tile of the drawable ancestor lands, which a second paint then lists. 'becomes display:none': the style change reaches the snapshot a frame after the test's single wait. Deterministic since 2026-10-16 (20 reps, 10 fresh-browser runs, quiet and with an idle Android Emulator): the first snapshot of the 8 drawables is one round, so the first paint is in the first frame; it used to take 4 rounds two frames apart and, depending on machine load, landed just before or just after the third subtest's change and then spilled into the fourth

onpaint-remove-non-drawable-element.tent.note: passes every subtest since 2026-10-16 (the first snapshot uses no credit of the snapshot-rate gate, so the rebuild after the first paint is in the next frame); before, the test's one-frame waits (rAF + setTimeout(0)) caught the paint only on a cold first load, and the file passed 4/4 or 0/4 by turns. Kept for the paint-timing deviation should a slower machine miss the single frame

onpaint.tentative.html.note: 'canvas ancestor changes': an attribute change on an ancestor damages every tile (the clone carries the ancestor shells, whose classes can restyle the content), so a paint with unchanged pixels follows; telling an unchanged tile apart needs a read-back of every rebuilt tile. The other 11 subtests pass in every rep. Three machine-load effects made this file flaky before 2026-10-16: a build that took 3.5 ms deferred its decode behind the test's next task (the grandchild paint then reached the next subtest's handler); the snapshot-rate gate compared post-frame task times with thresholds on whole 120 Hz frames; and its phase accumulator allowed a second build one frame after the first or not depending on the phase that the frame of the first build and dropped frames had left ('grandchild changes' or 'child transform' and 'drawing operations' failed by turns). Builds are now paced in frame time by a credit of builds
